title: Ithaca at Last

scenes.title: The Phaeacians Carry Odysseus Home
scenes.card: A friendly seafaring people sail the sleeping king home by night and leave him and his gifts on Ithaca's shore.

subs.text: Book thirteen.
Ithaca at Last.
Scene one.
The Phaeacians Carry Odysseus Home.
There, friends.
My story is told, and the telling has emptied me.
Bring out one more chest, and let every lord of Phaeacia add a tripod and a cauldron to it.
Then set the feast, for our guest sails at sundown and he must leave us glad.
At sunset Odysseus boards the convoy ship and lies on a prepared bed in the stern.
Swifter than a wheeling hawk the ship ran on,
and the man who had suffered twenty years of salt and war slept past all sorrow.
Before the dawn-star rose, her keel touched Ithaca.
The crew carries the sleeping man and his treasure onto the shore.

subs.text: Scene two.
Odysseus Wakes on an Unknown Shore.
What shore is this?
The ship is gone, and even the land has hidden its face from me.
Tripods, cauldrons, the woven robes, the gold.
All of it here, nothing taken.
Then why does this shore know nothing of me, unless those sailors dumped me on some foreign coast?
Wretched again, and among strangers again.
O Zeus, where do I carry all this wealth, and where do I carry myself?
Stranger, why do you wander this coast with treasure at your feet and fear in your eyes?

scenes.title: The Cretan Lie Meets Its Match
scenes.card: The goddess, disguised as a shepherd, tells him he is home; he lies about who he is, and she reveals herself.

subs.text: Scene three.
The Cretan Lie Meets Its Match.
The shepherd tells Odysseus you is in Ithaca and the hero suppresses your joy.
He invents a Cretan identity and a story of killing a king's son and fleeing by Phoenician ship.
Cunning, insatiable trickster, even in your own land you will not lay your lies aside!
Enough now:
I am Athena, daughter of Zeus, and we two are alike, crooked-minded both,
you the best of mortals at scheming and I of gods.
Hard goddess, where were you all the salt years since Troy burned?
You stood at my shoulder then, and after, I never once saw you on my deck while I suffered.
Now you come smiling and tell me this is Ithaca, so swear it is not one more mockery.
So that is the shape of it.
Poseidon's wrath made open rescue too costly, and you wore silence the way I wear rags.
You hid me even from my own eyes to keep me breathing.

scenes.title: The Treasure Is Hidden
scenes.card: Athena helps him hide his treasure in a cave and plan against the suitors; first he must go to his swineherd.

subs.text: Scene four.
The Treasure Is Hidden.
In with them.
Your bronze and gold will keep better here than on any beach.
There.
No thief alive will shift that stone.
Now sit with me under the olive, and let us plot.
Athena count the suitors and devise a concealment strategy.
Go first to your swineherd Eumaeus, keeper of your pigs and lover of your house,
and stay by his fire and question everything.
I go to Sparta, to fetch your son home.

scenes.world: A dim limestone sea cave and a single ancient olive tree on a misty Mediterranean hillside in soft grey light.

captain.asks: Plant the olive as a symbol: low wide of the two beneath it, then its trunk in insert, so the bed in XXIII can rhyme.

Best moments are the hand-drawn plan and the stone circle: planning is legible, concealment is not.

scenes.title: Athena Makes the Beggar
scenes.card: The goddess turns the king into a ragged old beggar so he can test his household without being recognized.

subs.text: Scene five.
Athena Makes the Beggar.
Athena touches Odysseus with her wand and shrivels his skin, hair, and limbs.
Dimmed eyes, wracked limbs, rags fit for burning on an old man's back.
No one who ever loved you will look at you twice.
Take this staff and this patched beggar's sack, for this is who you are now.
The transformed king is instructed to test servants without being recognized.
To Sparta, for the boy.
Walk on, old beggar, and keep to the high path.

captain.why: Bent figure on a rocky slope carries the old beggar's high path; light matches the grey cove.

sign.name: Limpid and opaque
sign.operation: Replacement on twos as the wand touches him: skin, hair, eyes, rags swapped one element at a time in one held medium.

scenes.world: A misty rocky hillside above a cove in flat grey morning light, the same olive and stone, one held frame of transformation.

captain.asks: Swap one element at a time in one held grey medium: hand, hair, eyes, rags, until the king is a beggar the woman leaves behind.
diagnosis: The transformation has no body to happen to: hands, eyes and faces belong to different strangers, so nothing is replaced, only shuffled.
The colour turbaned old man and the colour bearded man flood every row; refusing them keeps the medium but leaves the beggar thin.
Goddess and wand are never seen; the touch that drives the scene exists only in the voice.

prologue: Odysseus, king of the island of Ithaca, has been away twenty years: ten at war, ten lost at sea. Now a friendly people finally ship him home, but his house is overrun by men who court his wife and eat his wealth. He must come back in secret.
